issues.description: download_and_untar.sh warns about missing unzip but does not exit, then proceeds to call unzip
issues.detail: Lines 9-11 check `command -v unzip` and echo a warning, but lack an `exit`. The script then proceeds to the extraction blocks and dies on `unzip` with a cryptic 'command not found' rather than the intended preflight error. This is a textbook half-finished guard (DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE) — performs the social function of caring about errors without performing the logical function of preventing them. Add `exit 1` after the warning.

issues.description: download_and_untar.sh usage block prints help on bad argc but does not exit, falling through to realpath of unset $1
issues.detail: Lines 13-22 print a usage heredoc when `$#` is 0 or >2, but never `exit`. Under `set -u`, the next line `realpath $1` dies with an 'unbound variable' error instead of the helpful usage message just printed. The precondition (one or two positional args) is documented and then violated. Add `exit 1` after the heredoc.

issues.description: .complete sentinel files are touched inside directories assumed to be created by unzip, with no verification
issues.detail: `touch "$extract_dir/aisolution_data/.complete"` (and CH, MA variants) assumes each archive extracts to exactly that top-level directory name. If upstream layout drifts even slightly (nested folder, different case, re-zip by the third party), `touch` fails under `set -e`, leaving a partial extraction the next run cannot detect. Either verify the expected directory exists post-unzip with a clear error, or place the sentinel at `$extract_dir/.<archive>.complete` so it does not depend on archive-internal layout.

issues.description: data.sh cds into $TAL_ZH_ADULT_TEACH before download_and_untar.sh has guaranteed the directory exists
issues.detail: data.sh sources db.sh and then runs `TAL_ZH_ADULT_TEACH=$(cd "${TAL_ZH_ADULT_TEACH}"; pwd)`. The `cd` precondition (downloads directory exists) is supposed to be the postcondition of mkdir/download_and_untar.sh, but that script runs afterwards. With set -e, an absent `downloads/` kills data.sh before it can download anything. Order-of-operations is unreasoned.

issues.description: README links to a config path that does not exist in the diff
issues.detail: README writes `[./conf/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml](./conf/train/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml)` — the display text is correct but the href contains an extra `train/` segment. The actual file is at `conf/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml`. The headline artifact link 404s. Torvalds rates this P0; Knuth/Hickey/Liskov/Pike call it P2; Dijkstra P1 — see DISSENT.

issues.description: data.sh sources download_and_untar.sh via dot rather than executing it as a subprocess
issues.detail: `. ./local/download_and_untar.sh ...` collapses the module boundary: any `exit` inside the extractor terminates the parent, variables leak into the parent scope, and `set -euo pipefail` state is shared. Every other Kaldi/ESPnet recipe executes download_and_untar.sh as a child process. Replace with `./local/download_and_untar.sh ...` (or `bash ./local/...`) and check `$?`.

issues.description: Unquoted command substitutions in realpath calls break on paths with whitespace
issues.detail: `extract_dir=$(realpath $1)` and `zip_dir=$(realpath ${2:-$extract_dir})` do not quote their arguments. On paths containing spaces, realpath receives split args and silently picks the wrong directory; combined with `set -u`, this becomes a confusing foot-gun. Quote: `"$1"`, `"${2:-$extract_dir}"`.

issues.description: Three near-identical extraction blocks for TAL_ASR-1/2/3 — copy-paste begging to be a function or loop
issues.detail: Lines 28-58 are three 12-line stanzas differing only in (archive_name, sentinel_dir, human_name). Any bugfix must be applied in three places; the relationship between archive and output directory is implicit. Refactor to `extract_if_needed <zip_name> <sentinel_subdir>` called three times, or loop over a small data table.

issues.description: Transcript normalization is a chain of six sed substitutions with no stated postcondition
issues.detail: `sed 's/Ａ/A/g' | sed 's/#//g' | sed 's/=//g' | sed 's/、//g' | sed 's/，//g' | sed 's/？//g' | sed 's/。//g' | sed 's/[ ][ ]*$//g'` — no comment explains why these characters and not their half/full-width siblings (no 「」！：；…), why # and = appear (not Chinese punctuation), or what defines an accepted transcript. This is dataset-specific magic buried in pipeline code, complecting what to normalize with how to walk the file, and makes CER non-comparable across recipes. Pull the substitution table out as data, or define a Unicode-category-based normalizer, and document the invariant.

issues.description: Hardcoded utterance counts (22467/3208/6072/29386/38924) treat derived facts as literals
issues.detail: The here-doc at the bottom of data.sh asserts exact wav counts per split and exits if they disagree, with no comment citing dataset source, version, or verification date. The count is a derived property of the downloaded archive, not an input; encoding it as magic numbers freezes the recipe to one corpus snapshot and produces a confusing hard failure if upstream re-releases. Either compute the expected count from a shipped manifest, downgrade to a warning, or add a comment block with provenance.

issues.description: data.sh sources db.sh AFTER parse_options.sh, inverting the egs2 convention
issues.detail: Every other egs2 recipe sources db.sh/path.sh/cmd.sh BEFORE parse_options. Here it is reversed; works only because --downloads_dir does not reference any db var, but breaks the convention reviewers and future maintainers expect. Match the existing codebase style.

issues.description: data.sh overwrites utt.list mid-pipeline, reusing the same filename for two different roles
issues.detail: Line 41 creates utt.list from wav.flist; line 51 overwrites utt.list with filtered transcript keys. Same filename, different semantics, race-prone under reruns and confusing on read. Use distinct names (utt.list.wav, utt.list.txt).

issues.description: prepare_kaldi's contract is implicit and tightly coupled to directory depth and basename uniqueness
issues.detail: prepare_kaldi(name, wav_subdir, transcript, expected_count) silently depends on: every basename in wav.flist being unique within its directory (otherwise `sort -u -k 1` drops duplicates and rows misalign), the third path component from leaf encoding the speaker (`TALASR$(NF-1)`), and the transcript being keyed by basename-of-wav. None of this is documented or asserted; an extra wrapper directory or duplicate basename silently corrupts the dataset and is masked by fix_data_dir.sh. State preconditions at the top of the function and assert basename-uniqueness with `sort | uniq -d | wc -l`.

issues.description: The num_wav check accuses 'text' of mismatching expected when the root cause may be the wav side
issues.detail: prepare_kaldi compares text-line count against expected num_wav, but the data was filtered through filter_scp against the transcript. If the trans file lacks rows for some wavs (or has rows for absent wavs), the diagnostic blames text when wav is the real problem. The invariant being checked is not the invariant the author thinks they are checking.

issues.description: Bare-dot YAML floats (`0.`) in train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml
issues.detail: `self_attention_dropout_rate: 0.`, `src_attention_dropout_rate: 0.`, and `time_mask_width_ratio_range: - 0.` — PyYAML parses as 0.0 but the bare-dot form is visually ambiguous (typo for 0.1?) and may break stricter parsers/linters. Write `0.0`. Knuth and Torvalds rate P2; Dijkstra rates P1.

issues.description: decode_asr_branchformer.yaml sets lm_weight: 0.7 but run.sh defaults use_lm=false
issues.detail: The LM weight is dead on the default code path. Published LM-decoding numbers in the README imply the recipe is meant to be run with use_lm=true. Either flip the run.sh default or document on the README that the LM numbers require `--use_lm true`.

issues.description: local/path.sh duplicates MAIN_ROOT already provided by the symlinked TEMPLATE/asr1/path.sh
issues.detail: egs2/tal_zh_adult_teach/asr1/local/path.sh contains only `MAIN_ROOT=$PWD/../../..`, while a top-level path.sh symlink to TEMPLATE/asr1/path.sh already exists. Two paths to the same fact, no documented precedence — textbook complecting of configuration and location. Either delete local/path.sh or document why both exist.

issues.description: --downloads_dir is parsed but dead
issues.detail: data.sh accepts `--downloads_dir` via parse_options.sh but never uses `${downloads_dir}` directly beyond a dot-sourced call into download_and_untar.sh. Default-empty silently makes `zip_dir=$extract_dir`. Either remove the option or thread it through and document the default.

issues.description: download_and_untar.sh empty-string vs unset handling of $2 fallback is ambiguous
issues.detail: `zip_dir=$(realpath ${2:-$extract_dir})` triggers the fallback only when `$2` is unset, not when it is empty. Passing an empty `downloads_dir` makes realpath of '' return cwd, masking the intended fallback. Use explicit check: `zip_dir=${2:-$extract_dir}; [ -z "$zip_dir" ] && zip_dir=$extract_dir`.

issues.description: wav.flist is re-parsed three times instead of once
issues.detail: data.sh runs effectively the same `sed | awk` pipeline over wav.flist three times to produce utt.list, utt_uttid, and utt2spk. A single awk pass can emit all three via `print ... > file` redirections. Pick the data structure once and the algorithm becomes obvious.

issues.description: Comments contain casual typos and stray characters
issues.detail: train_lm_transformer.yaml: `# 15epoch is enougth` (enough), `# 10 is good.`. cmd.sh: trailing `=========================================================~` with a tilde. Configs become reference docs; the comments are part of the artifact.

issues.description: Speaker ID derived from directory name (TALASR$(NF-1)) — directory proxy, not real speaker
issues.detail: Despite the PR description citing 80+ speakers, data.sh sets the speaker to the parent folder, making every directory a 'speaker.' Fine as a modelling choice for plain ASR, but it complects 'speaker identity' with 'directory layout' and will surprise a future user expecting real speaker labels for SpecAugment or adaptation. Add a one-line comment in data.sh saying spk is a directory proxy.

issues.description: Inline punctuation scrubs should live in a named filter rather than buried mid-pipeline
issues.detail: The seven CJK-punctuation substitutions are dataset-specific normalization buried in data.sh. Moving them into a `local/normalize_text.sh` (or one `python -c` call) makes the transform reusable and keeps data.sh as a pipeline of clearly named steps.

issues.description: Committed symlinks lack trailing newlines ('\ No newline at end of file')
issues.detail: asr.sh, db.sh, path.sh, pyscripts, scripts, steps, utils all show the git warning. Cosmetic and conventional for symlinks, but worth noting as a sign the diff was assembled rather than authored.

issues.description: Termination/shrinkage invariant for prepare_kaldi's filter chain is not stated
issues.detail: prepare_kaldi runs records through sorted joins and filter_scp; the invariant 'utt.list always shrinks or stays the same under each filter' is not written down. State it in a comment so the next maintainer is not forced to reconstruct it.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a standard ESPnet egs2 recipe addition whose model side is conventional and whose problems concentrate in two shell scripts: local/download_and_untar.sh and local/data.sh. The strongest universally-flagged finding (all six reviewers) is the half-finished unzip-missing guard that warns and then proceeds; five of six also flag the usage block that prints help and falls through to `realpath $1` under set -u. Three reviewers (Knuth, Torvalds, Dijkstra) further flag that .complete sentinels are touched inside directories that unzip is merely assumed to have produced. The strongest preserved disagreement is on severity: Torvalds and Dijkstra rate the missing-exit bugs and (for Torvalds) the broken README link as P0 outright blockers, while Knuth/Hickey/Liskov/Pike treat them as P1 fix-before-merge or P2 cosmetic. Dijkstra alone flags a P0 ordering bug where data.sh cds into $TAL_ZH_ADULT_TEACH before downloads/ is guaranteed to exist, and Hickey/Liskov alone flag the lm_weight vs use_lm=false inconsistency — minority concerns preserved per protocol.
